description: Percona Search for MongoDB (mongot) - full-text ($search) and vector ($vectorSearch) search health, replication, query performance, Lucene storage, JVM and system resources.

panels.title: mongot Services Down
panels.description: Number of selected mongot services PMM cannot scrape (up == 0). See the Search Services table for which one.

panels.title: Indexes Not STEADY
panels.description: Indexes on the selected services whose status is not STEADY (FAILED, DOES_NOT_EXIST, INITIAL_SYNC, RECOVERING_*, NOT_STARTED, STALE). The Search Indexes table lists them first.

panels.title: Worst Replication Lag
panels.description: Highest per-index replication lag across the selected services. Should be close to 0 in steady state; rising lag means search results are stale.

panels.title: Lowest Data Path Free
panels.description: Lowest free space on a mongot data path (storage.dataPath) among the selected services. mongot pauses replication at 90% used (10% free) and resumes at 85% used. See the Search Services table for which service.

panels.title: $search/s
panels.description: $search commands per second across the selected services.

panels.title: $vectorSearch/s
panels.description: $vectorSearch commands per second across the selected services.

panels.title: Highest Heap Used
panels.description: Highest JVM heap usage (% of max heap) among the selected services. Pools without a configured max (-1) are excluded.

panels.title: Shortest Uptime
panels.description: Uptime of the most recently (re)started mongot among the selected services. A small value means a service restarted.

panels.title: Search Services
panels.description: One row per mongot service with its node, cluster and replica set, and the signals that need attention. Status is whether PMM can scrape mongot's metrics endpoint. Per-service query rates are in the Query Performance row.

panels.title: Search Indexes
panels.description: One row per search / vector search index per mongot service, problems first (sorted by Status, then use the column headers). Indexes are identified by ObjectId: mongot metrics carry no index, database or collection name; map an ID with db.<collection>.getSearchIndexes() (field 'id'). The footer shows the number of rows.

panels.title: Index Status by Service
panels.description: Number of indexes in each status on each mongot service. Anything other than STEADY for a sustained period needs attention; FAILED or DOES_NOT_EXIST should alert.

panels.title: Replication Index Manager State
panels.description: Index managers in each state of mongot's replication state machine, per service. Expected: STEADY_STATE. FAILED / FAILED_EXCEEDED need attention; STEADY_STATE_SHUT_DOWN appears while mongod is unreachable.

panels.title: Index Lifecycle
panels.description: Indexes in catalog, still initializing (should return to 0 after startup) and being phased out, per service.

panels.title: Index Lifecycle Failures
panels.description: Failed index initializations, downloads and drops per service. Any increase should be investigated immediately.

panels.title: Max Replication Lag per Service
panels.description: Highest index replication lag on each mongot service. Should be ~0 in steady state.

panels.title: Replication Lag (top 10 indexes)
panels.description: The 10 indexes with the highest replication lag at each point in time. Use the Index ID filter to follow a specific index.

panels.title: Replication Exceptions
panels.description: Exceptions in mongot's replication index manager per service, and the 10 indexes with the most initial-sync / steady-state exceptions. Any steady-state exception should be investigated; a sustained consecutive resync count means an index is stuck in a retry loop.

panels.title: Index Operations
panels.description: Document inserts, updates and deletes applied to search indexes from the change stream, per service.

panels.title: Change Stream
panels.description: Change stream getMores in flight, batches in progress and unexpected batch failures (alert on any failure) per service. Large events (>10 MiB) may signal abnormal document sizes.

panels.title: Search Command Rate
panels.description: $search, $vectorSearch and getMore commands handled by each mongot service.

panels.title: Search Command Errors
panels.description: Failed and invalid commands/queries per service. Command failures are user-visible errors; internally failed queries are mongot-side failures; invalid queries were rejected as malformed. When mongot is hung or unreachable these stay at 0 - check 'mongod to mongot Streams' instead.

panels.title: $search Latency
panels.description: End-to-end $search command latency per mongot service. Quantiles are computed by mongot (Prometheus summary, sliding window).

panels.title: $vectorSearch Latency
panels.description: End-to-end $vectorSearch command latency per mongot service. Quantiles are computed by mongot (Prometheus summary, sliding window).

panels.title: Lucene Search Latency (P99)
panels.description: P99 time spent in Lucene collecting top documents for $search and $vectorSearch, per service.

panels.title: Queries per Index (top 10)
panels.description: Query throughput of the 10 busiest indexes.

panels.title: $vectorSearch Query Types
panels.description: Approximate (HNSW) vs exact (ENN) vector queries per service.

panels.title: HNSW Nodes Visited per Query
panels.description: Average HNSW graph nodes visited per $vectorSearch query, per service. Higher means more expensive vector queries.

panels.title: Open Cursors
panels.description: Cursors tracked by each mongot service. Sustained growth may indicate a cursor leak.

panels.title: Search Stages Executed on mongod
panels.description: $search, $searchMeta and $vectorSearch aggregation stages executed by each mongod (from mongodb_exporter). If mongod runs search stages but mongot reports no commands, requests are not reaching mongot.

panels.title: mongod to mongot Streams
panels.description: gRPC streams from each mongod to its mongot. Failed streams, or active streams that never finish, mean mongot is unreachable or hung: queries wait until maxTimeMS and fail on the client side even though mongot reports no failed commands.

panels.title: mongod to mongot Connection Pool
panels.description: Each mongod's connection pool to mongot (used when gRPC is disabled). Pending or rejected requests mean mongod cannot get a connection to mongot.

panels.title: mongod to mongot Request Time
panels.description: Average time each mongod's mongot executor tasks wait to be scheduled and run.

panels.title: Indexing Queue
panels.description: Pending indexing and decoding work per service. Sustained non-zero values mean an indexing backlog: mongot cannot keep up with the write rate.

panels.title: Batch Durations
panels.description: Average time to process an indexing and a decoding batch, per service.

panels.title: Index Commit Duration (top 10)
panels.description: Average Lucene commit time of the 10 slowest indexes.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (service_name, indexId_logString) (rate(mongot_index_stats_indexing_commitDurations_seconds_sum{service_name=~"$service_name",indexId_logString=~"$index"})) / sum by (service_name, indexId_logString) (rate(mongot_index_stats_indexing_commitDurations_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service_name",indexId_logString=~"$index"})))

panels.title: Batch Duration by Index Type
panels.description: Average indexing batch duration per service and index type.

targets.expr: sum by (service_name, indexType) (rate(mongot_index_stats_indexing_indexingBatchDurations_seconds_sum{service_name=~"$service_name"})) / sum by (service_name, indexType) (rate(mongot_index_stats_indexing_indexingBatchDurations_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service_name"}))

panels.title: Total Index Size per Service
panels.description: Total size of all indexes on disk, and the memory mongot estimates they need to be fully cached, per service.

panels.title: Largest Indexes (top 10)
panels.description: On-disk size of the 10 largest indexes.

panels.title: Segments per Index (top 10)
panels.description: Lucene segment count of the 10 indexes with the most segments. Very high counts (100+) indicate a merge policy problem.

panels.title: Merge Activity
panels.description: Running Lucene merges per service. A sustained high value means a merge storm. Aborted merges indicate resource pressure; discarded merges were skipped due to disk pressure (alert on any).

panels.title: Merge Time
panels.description: Average and maximum duration of a Lucene merge, per service.

panels.title: JVM Heap
panels.description: Heap used, live data after GC, and max heap per service. A sustained upward trend can precede OutOfMemory.

panels.title: GC Pause Time
panels.description: Time spent in GC pauses per second and the maximum pause, per service. High pauses degrade query latency.

panels.title: GC Frequency
panels.description: GC pauses per second, per service and collector. Frequent minor GCs indicate memory pressure.

panels.title: Off-heap Buffers
panels.description: Direct buffers and memory-mapped Lucene index files per service. Mapped memory grows with index size.

panels.title: CPU Usage
panels.description: CPU used by the mongot JVM process and by the whole host, per service. Spikes correlate with merge storms or query overload.

panels.title: Load Average
panels.description: Host 1-minute load average reported by each mongot service, and its CPU count.

panels.title: Available Memory
panels.description: Physical memory available on each mongot host. Low available memory causes Lucene files to be evicted from the page cache.

panels.title: Data Path Free Space
panels.description: Free space on each mongot data path. mongot pauses replication at 90% used, resumes at 85%, and skips merges under disk pressure.

panels.title: Disk Queue Length
panels.description: Maximum disk I/O queue depth on each mongot host. Sustained > 1 indicates a disk bottleneck.

panels.title: Major Page Faults
panels.description: Major page faults (reads from disk) of each mongot process. Rising major faults mean index files do not fit in memory.

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Connections held by each internal mongot MongoDB client, per service.

panels.title: Connections Checked Out (% of max)
panels.description: Connections in use as a percentage of each pool's maxSize, per service. Approaching 100% means pool exhaustion.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (service_name, clientName) (mongot_mongoClient_connectionPool_connectionsCheckedOut{service_name=~"$service_name"}) / sum by (service_name, clientName) (mongot_mongoClient_connectionPool_maxSize{service_name=~"$service_name"} > 0) > 0

title: MongoDB Search Details
